capabilities.evidence: RealtimeTextPane + RealtimeTextSessionModel send/receive over text/1-negotiated kind-9 frames; RealtimeTextFrameTests/RealtimeTextSessionModelTests cover wire interop, consent gating, and history limits

Send: one shared expandSelection/SelectionStore behind all three send flows (DirectPane pairing code, NearbyPane same-network, UploadPane cloud). Folders recurse depth-first in a deterministic, locale-independent UTF-8 order, the selected folder's own name is kept, and MAX_FILES, the per-path byte bound and the sealed-BATCH-frame size are all enforced BEFORE a connection is opened or an upload starts. Symlinks are refused by name rather than followed (could send files from outside the selection) or skipped (would send an incomplete tree silently), which also removes the cycle question. Wire: realtime sends populate FileMeta.path exactly as the web does (leaf in name, folder-relative path in path, path absent for a loose file); cloud sends reuse the FROZEN stored manifest by putting the forward-slash relative path in ManifestFile.name — the convention the Go CLI's walkUploadPaths has always emitted and safeJoin has always read — so no new field, no golden-vector change, and old flat manifests are untouched. Receive: ManifestWriter rebuilds safe nested trees for both transports, treating every manifest path as hostile — absolute/traversal/dot/empty segments refused (not repaired), per-segment control+bidi stripping, canonical+case-insensitive duplicate refusal, file-vs-directory prefix refusal, pre-existing target refusal, and cleanup of partial files plus only the directories it created — never the user-chosen parent. The write path is descriptor-relative (openat/mkdirat/fstatat/unlinkat), not path-based: the destination is opened once, every component is walked with O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY from the previous component's descriptor, the leaf is taken with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, and the bytes go through the descriptor that call returned — never a reopen by name. The leaf is genuinely single-lookup — O_CREAT|O_EXCL decides and takes the name in one syscall, and every byte afterwards goes through that descriptor. Directory creation does name a component twice (mkdirat then openat); what makes that safe is not a single lookup but exclusive creation plus O_NOFOLLOW on the open, so a swap in between fails the open rather than redirecting it. The property is CONTAINMENT — a lost race is a refusal, never a write outside the destination — not the absence of races. Cleanup of files and subdirectories is confined the same way and uses AT_REMOVEDIR, so 'only while empty' is enforced by the kernel rather than by a losable check. ONE cleanup step is not fully descriptor-relative and is stated exactly rather than glossed: removing the transfer's own container requires naming it in its parent, since macOS has no 'remove the directory this descriptor refers to'. A container this transfer creates is therefore created and PINNED together (createOwnedContainer: mkdirat then openat O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY), the writer takes a dup of that descriptor rather than reopening the path, and every removal compares the name's (st_dev, st_ino) against that ORIGINAL pinned descriptor. Pinning at creation is the load-bearing part: an earlier version opened the container's path inside its own failure handler, which pinned whatever was there at that moment and then compared it against itself — it would have deleted an empty replacement while reading, in review, as a careful identity check. Under ambiguous identity the rule is to LEAK an empty directory (ours, now unreachable by name) rather than delete a replacement. Residual windows, not claimed away: (a) create-to-pin, between mkdirat and openat — a symlink or plain file swapped in there fails the open, but a real DIRECTORY swapped in there does not: it is pinned in place of ours and the transfer writes into it; (b) a swap landing between the identity fstatat and the unlinkat, which at worst removes an attacker's own EMPTY directory (AT_REMOVEDIR refuses a symlink with ENOTDIR and a non-empty directory with ENOTEMPTY, so no data is destroyed). The guarantee is stated as what it is and NOT as containment by location: path lookups cannot be REDIRECTED (a name swapped after its descriptor was opened does not move the operation anchored to it, symlinks fail rather than being followed) and cleanup whose name no longer resolves to the pinned inode leaves that name alone. It is NOT 'nothing lands outside the folder the user chose' — a descriptor pins an inode, not a location, so an actor with write access to the parent can rename the pinned directory anywhere and subsequent writes follow it there; testAPinnedContainerKeepsWorkingAfterItsNameChanges asserts exactly that behaviour rather than pretending otherwise. A folder receive gets its own container named after the sent folder (stepping aside to "name (2)", never merging), with the root lifted out so the tree gains no level; a one-file folder keeps its folder by the same rule. Staged sends are pinned by descriptor: FileURLSource opens each selected file once at staging (O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, fstat-verified regular file) and reads it with pread through that descriptor, so replacing the final component, replacing a directory above it, or substituting a file of exactly the same size between consent and transmission cannot change the bytes sent. The descriptor is owned by a class, so ARC releases it whenever a staged batch is dropped. Every descriptor the receive path holds on a destination or a file in it is close-on-exec, including the container duplicate — dup(2) does not copy FD_CLOEXEC, so that one goes through F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC, and a test walks the process's own open descriptors (F_GETPATH) to assert none pointing into a live receive is inheritable by a child process. A completed file is fsync'd before it counts as written and a FAILED sync fails the transfer (errno captured before the close that follows), rather than being swallowed as it briefly was — a full disk must not produce a transfer reported complete whose bytes are not on disk. Retrying a session inherits nothing from the one it replaced: the connection, the SAS, the DataChannel-open flag, any pending receive and its manifest are all released, so a retry must reach readiness on its own two callbacks in either order and cannot install or ACCEPT the previous peer's manifest; the staged OUTBOUND selection and its byte total are deliberately preserved, a partial receive's debris is discarded, and a completed receive's files are kept. A rejected manifest never leaves its container behind, on the cloud multi-flat path as well as the nested one — proved end to end through CloudDownloadModel against a stubbed server, not only on the helper it delegates to. Evidence: FileSelectionTests (22), FolderReceiveTests (26), ManifestWriterRaceTests (18), StagedSourcePinningTests (13), SelectionStoreTests (11), CloudDownloadModelTests (16) + CloudDownloadModelContainerTests (2, one of which downloads a real ciphertext blob end to end and asserts the container and its files), 9 folder/retry/lifecycle cases in RealtimeSessionModelTests, ErrorCopy coverage for every refusal; 573 Swift tests green. The race and pinning tests drive test-only hooks that perform the worst-case swap in the exact syscall window, and are mutation-checked: reverting to reopen-by-path fails 4, dropping O_NOFOLLOW fails 3, dropping O_EXCL fails 3, dropping the regular-file check fails 2, removing the descriptor-owning deinit fails 1, ignoring the fsync result fails 2, removing the container identity check fails 1, leaving SAS/open state across a retry fails 3, leaving the pending receive across a retry fails 3, removing the negative-sum guard reproduces the process trap, reopening the container by path in the cleanup handler fails 2, dropping the identity comparison fails 3, removing BOTH container-cleanup layers fails the end-to-end cloud test, and replacing F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC with a bare dup fails the inheritance test. Interop is pinned by value on both sides: server/internal/cloud/transfer_folder_interop_test.go asserts the same walk order, the same byte-exact manifest JSON, and that a native-shaped folder manifest lands as a real tree in the Go CLI; StoredManifestTests asserts the identical JSON literal. Web consumer fixed to match (DownloadPage splits a slashed name into {name, path}, so a native/CLI folder now reaches the ZIP sink instead of being flattened by per-file blob downloads on Firefox/Safari/mobile). Caveats on the race work specifically: the property is CONTAINMENT — an attacker who wins a race causes a refusal, never a redirect outside the destination — and it does not stop a process that can already write inside the destination, or that can modify a selected file's contents in place through the very inode that was pinned (bounded instead by the per-file chained hash the receiver verifies and by the grown/shrunk-source refusal). Other caveats: an EMPTY directory cannot be sent at all — neither wire format has an entry for a directory — so it is reported in the pane's summary rather than silently dropped; hidden files (.DS_Store) ARE included, matching the Go CLI; backslash is treated as an ordinary Darwin filename character, not a separator, so a name containing one materialises as one inert file here but is split by the web's ZIP sink; the panes themselves are exercised only through their models, and no signed-Release build has been driven by hand

Both directions. Outgoing: NearbyPane + LanDiscoveryModel join the code-less room (STUN-only /api/ice, no mint, no auth, works signed out) and send files or text to a device the user picks by peer id; LanDiscoveryTests/NearbyTransferTests cover self-exclusion, no auto-select, duplicate names, stale selection and TURN exclusion. Incoming: NearbyReceiveModel answers an unsolicited file or text offer through the real RealtimeSessionModel/RealtimeTextSessionModel responder paths, with the same STUN-only, no-mint, no-token guarantees (RealtimeConnectionFactory.acceptNearby + nearbyICEServers). NearbyReceiveTests/InboundGateTests cover one-session-at-a-time admission, generation-tagged busy replies, buffer-and-replay ordering, exactly-once routing (including a duplicate offer during setup being dropped rather than replayed or refused), glare refusal from the live peer, reservation release on every failure path, a stale attempt from a replaced socket neither building nor reporting over the session that succeeded it, and sequential passive sessions. Live evidence: in-process production E2E (Sources/NearbyReceiveE2E) PASS for file then text against relayium.com, bytes and SAS compared on BOTH sides. Caveats: only advanced verification (off by default) ever establishes who the peer is, and the room is keyed by the server-observed public IP, so anything sharing that address can offer — disclosed in NearbyPane and pausable. Not covered by any automated test: the pane and menu-bar surfaces themselves, which are exercised only through their models

LanDiscoveryModel.startResident keeps one room socket for the life of the process (MenuBarExtra keeps that process up), reconnects on bounded backoff, and honours a sticky user pause. NearbyReceiveModel re-subscribes on every socket via NearbyRoomObserver, so a reconnect does not silently end reachability, and reports off/paused/connecting/reconnecting/active truthfully rather than claiming ready — connecting is distinct because before the hub's welcome this Mac has no peer id and is in nobody's roster. Covered by NearbyReceiveTests (listener follows the socket across a reconnect, a paused listener answers nothing, reconnecting and connecting are reported as such) and LanDiscoveryTests. A prior session also confirmed a live shipped-bundle receive: NearbyReceiveE2E --send-to against a running Relayium.app answered a passive file offer with nothing clicked. Caveat: that live-app run used a Debug build launched from DerivedData and has NOT been repeated since the routing/ownership fixes in this round; the equivalent path is re-covered in-process and by unit tests, but a signed Release build has never been exercised this way
AccountView shows plan/usage only; device and stored-file management remain web-only

Drag-in: one FileDropZone and one picker (canChooseDirectories = true) behind all three send flows, replacing the cloud pane's file-only drop and the two realtime panes' folder-rejecting pickers. A drop STAGES and never sends — on NearbyPane the zone sits above and independent of the roster, so a drop cannot pick or dial a device, and sendFiles re-reads the live selection and guards on busy so a second press cannot start duplicate work. Drops append with root de-duplication (dropping the same folder twice is a no-op); the picker replaces, because the panel is a moment of confirmation a drag does not have. The zone renders but declines while busy rather than vanishing mid-drag. Drag-out: ReceivedResultView offers NSItemProvider(contentsOf:) file URLs for every successfully received realtime and cloud item, built ONLY from receivedPayload, which is only reachable in .completed/.done — i.e. after the writer's finish() returned — so no URL is offered before it is complete and closed. A foldered result offers its container as the single drag item, because dragging the individual files would flatten the tree at the destination. Reveal in Finder is kept on both surfaces and now selects the container for a folder result. Decisions live in RelayiumAppKit (SelectionStore, receivedPayload) and are covered by SelectionStoreTests and FolderReceiveTests' payload cases; the SwiftUI files hold no decisions. Drop decoding accepts every representation public.file-url is actually vended as — Data, URL, NSURL, NSData, String, NSString — rather than only Data, which silently ignored drags from apps that vend an NSURL; non-file URLs and bare paths are rejected, and the result is canonicalised so NSURL's trailing slash for a directory and Data's lack of one cannot stage one folder twice (droppedFileURL, covered by SelectionStoreTests). Sandbox: powerbox issues an implicit process-lifetime extension for picker- and drag-supplied URLs, so staging can enumerate now and open afterwards; readability is not merely probed but HELD — FileURLSource keeps each selected file's descriptor from staging until the batch is released — so an unreadable selection fails before a connection is opened and the staged bytes cannot be swapped while a transfer waits for a peer. Caveats: the drag-out gesture itself and the drop gesture itself are AppKit/SwiftUI surfaces with no automated coverage — only the URL payload seam and the staging decisions behind them are tested — and neither has been exercised by hand in a signed Release build
